title: Intelligent Applications Based on Medical Large Models to Enhance People's Healthcare Experience and Health Status
summary: Ant Group reports that its medical AI assistant, later the AQ app, reached over 13 million users and that its annotation system improved efficiency by 50%; no health effect is reported.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: In a submission to the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), Alipay describes medical assistants for residents, clinicians and underserved areas. The submission reports that, since its launch in June 2024, the service has reached over 13 million users and delivered more than 78 million service instances. It reports a 98% user satisfaction rate. It also reports a 50% improvement in annotation efficiency from an annotation system developed with specialist doctors, and it gives no baseline figure. The submission names improved health and a more equitable distribution of care as broader intended benefits. Ant released the assistant as a standalone app, AQ, on 26 June 2025. Ant renamed it Ant Afu on 15 December 2025, when Xinhua reported Ant's figure of more than 15 million monthly users. In January 2026 the Economic Observer reported more than 30 million monthly users without naming a source for the figure. No source reports a measured effect on users' health.
purpose: Provide medical guidance and reduce administrative and information-processing work.
system: Ant medical large model and health-assistant agents
deployer: Zhejiang Provincial Health Commission; Hangzhou Municipal Medical Insurance Bureau; Renji Hospital
